- The same four test files on a `git archive cf522df` copy -> 107 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail, so the commit itself is green.

findings:
- Non-blocking, `packages/runtime/src/setup/settings.ts:42-43`. The entry is keyed to the canonical `claude-opus-5-5` while the root runs `model: opus`, an alias. When the alias moves to a newer Opus, setup and doctor still report success and the root silently loses high effort and the 200k window. Doctor cannot detect this.
- Non-blocking, `settings.ts:42-43`. Because doctor checks for a missing key, a user who runs `/effort auto` to clear their level gets a doctor FAIL until `--fix` re-adds `high`. Setup itself only adds missing keys, so it never overwrites a value the user set.
- Non-blocking, `packages/integrations/claude/src/agents.ts:475-478`. The comment cites anthropics/claude-code#81677 and #97829 for "ignored on the main thread". I could not verify those issue numbers. The settings reference and sub-agents docs say only that frontmatter `effort` applies when the subagent is active; they do not mention the main thread.
- Non-blocking, `packages/runtime/tests/setup.test.ts` (the "this repository's settings" test). Its expected value comes from `applyDefaults(userSettingsDefaults)`, so it only catches drift between the repo file and the defaults. The literal values are pinned by the other tests, so the pair is adequate.
- Non-blocking, `packages/integrations/claude/tests/plugin.test.ts`. The new root tests assert about 20 `includes()` phrases of instruction wording. This matches the file's existing style, but it couples tests to wording.
- Non-blocking, `.claude/settings.json:6-8`. The entry applies only on Opus 5.5. This session runs Sonnet 5.5, so it gets neither effort nor window. That is by design for the root, not a defect.
- The `/code-review` findings on instruction text are outside my scope (`context.md`, `version-control.md`, `asking.md`, `visual.md` wording, `ci.md`). I did not verify them in depth and leave them to the instruction reviewer. Two I checked against code:
  - The `.claude/settings.json` model-key finding is rejected as by design (see above).
  - The R-VISUAL phrase loosening is only the text of the requirement, and the test pins it.

verified (checked against code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md, fetched 2026-11-02):
- `modelSettings` is keyed by canonical model name, such as `claude-opus-5-5`. Claude Code matches that model's alias, dated and `[1m]` IDs to the same entry.
- `effortLevel` takes `low`, `medium`, `high` or `xhigh`, so `high` is valid.
- `autoCompactWindow` takes 100000 to 1000000 or `"auto"`, so 200000 is valid. The per-model form needs Claude Code v2.1.288 or later, and `modelSettings` itself needs v2.1.251 or later.
- A top-level `effortLevel` in user settings is ignored on Opus 5.5, so the per-model entry is the correct form.
- `modelSettings` has scope "Any file", so the project `.claude/settings.json` may carry it.
- Frontmatter `effort: high` is a valid sub-agents field value. The generated `dist/agents/holyagent.md` has it between `model: opus` and `disallowedTools`.
- `applyDefaults` and `place` never overwrite an existing leaf. A non-object where an object is needed is kept, and sibling model entries such as `claude-sonnet-5-5: {}` survive. The keep-user-value test covers an existing `xhigh`.
- The two new keys raise the setup-cli counts from 8 to 10 (leaf paths: effortLevel and autoCompactWindow). That is exact and not loosened.
- `.claude/settings.json` gains only the `modelSettings` block. Every other key is unchanged, and it is valid JSON.
- Doctor exit codes are unchanged. It fails only when a key is missing, as with the earlier keys.

Not run: the full `mise run verify` (shared tree is moving), and Claude Code itself reading the settings (docs read only).
